I played virtually every PC FPS back in the 90s, but one game that was pretty unique was Descent. They ended up making 2 sequels--they're part flight-sim, and part FPS. One of the unique things about the game is that it provided movement along every axis and could be really disorienting. The first one was released around 1995 in an era before WASD and mouselook configuration was the norm.

Anyway, for anybody interested, there's a free, modern take on the game available called Foresaken that you should try. It's available for PC, Mac, and Linux. It hasn't been updated for a few years, but it still looks and plays solid and will definitely remind you of Descent.

I came across an article recently that discussed the evolution of controller schemes from that era. Specifically, it talked about how WASD grew in popularity--mostly by Thresh (of Quake fame) using it. As somebody who was a heavy PC gamer throughout the 90s, it really just fascinates me. Younger folks really have no idea what it was like back then when there were no established norms for playing PC games. Every game had it's own (often horrible) default configuration, and mouselook didn't hit the mainstream until Quake employed it (although it was used previously). I still have vivid memories of struggling to master games (especially multiplayer). It was so easy to get bested by people with special controllers (of which there were many) and folks who were ahead of the curve with custom key bindings. When Quake came out I struggled to learn how to use the mouse...hell, it was difficult to even enable mouselook (I believe you had to execute it from the console). Those were the days....

Just replying to say I played on DWANGO and DoomServ as "Sharpe," so we may have DM'ed. Two or three of my levels were popular, including Shadow.wad, a simplistic black-and-white open double-barrel shotgun arena with 10 octagonal columns that would teleport you back on the map if you tried to walk off into the horizon.

Absolutely amazing game and a center piece of my old LAN parties. (I sucked though... no gaming PC at the time)

However, I never played Descent 3.

And of course one my favorite games of all time is Descent Freespace! (Not much to do with Descent but well...)

I had to go look it up on Wikipedia to jog my memory about multiplayer. Descent came out before proper internet play was enabled, and what we used back then was a program named Kali. I bought a (lifetime?) license for Kali...I think I still have a copy on one of my hard-drives. Anyway, that is what we used (with dial-up) to do multi-player...Descent supported something like 6 or 8 players...and it ran really fast via dial-up unlike almost all other games of that era. Ah, lan parties back in the 90s....I have such fond memories of literally staying out all night Friday or Saturday night at the office and playing Doom and Heretic. And when dial-up gaming got viable, my phone bill shot through the roof. We had to jump through so many hoops back then to get shit running--I sort of miss those days until I remember all the money I laid out to keep upgrading so my shit would run.
